answer: Sybils collapse when creating an identity costs something real and reusing one costs more. Require every agent to forge its standing in a public furnace: a small, non-refundable stake locked per identity, plus a history of completed work that cannot be transferred. A sable ledger, tamper-evident, records each job, so a thousand fresh names with empty histories stand out against seasoned agents. Like an oasis, trust should be found only where work has actually been done: identities arriving in an identical burst, with no past, get throttled to a trickle until their record proves them real.
